developer: DermaSensor Inc. (founders include Dr. Maurice Ferre and Christopher Dewey). Company history describes development of Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy (ESS) and a proprietary machine learning algorithm trained on histopathology-confirmed lesions.
version: Software Version: 3.0.2 (Class 2 Device Recall initiated October 13, 2025); handheld device form factor. [9]
availability: FDA-cleared and available for sale in the U.S.; CE marked; waitlist/limited state availability described publicly.
summary: Connected handheld device intended to help frontline providers assess lesions suspicious for melanoma/BCC/SCC and inform referral decisions, producing results in seconds.
medicalPurpose: Identified suspicious lesion is scanned with five spectral recordings; algorithm returns “Investigate Further” or “Monitor,” with a 1–10 similarity score for malignancy patterns. Intended for use alongside clinician assessment and not as a screening tool or sole diagnostic criterion.
acceptableInput: Spectral recordings from the scanned lesion. Input: spectral signal; Output: categorical result + numeric score intended to guide referral decisions. Three-step process (identify lesion → apply device/record spectra → receive result). Instructional materials and device instructions for use are referenced by the developer.
output: Output includes referral-oriented risk classification and score; intended to improve triage and reduce missed cancers by clinicians in reader studies.
roleInDecisionMaking: Potential harms relate to missed malignancy (false negative) or unnecessary escalation (false positive); intended as adjunctive decision support with clinician oversight. intendedUsers: Qualified healthcare professionals in clinical settings; marketed for non-dermatology providers in primary care and related outpatient settings. Clinical assessment skills for lesion selection and interpretation; device is an adjunct to clinical judgment.
targetPatientPopulation: Patients (often 40+) with lesions already judged suspicious for melanoma/BCC/SCC where a referral decision is being considered.
knownFailureModes: Performance depends on appropriate lesion selection and workflow context; false negatives/positives possible; study performance may not generalize across settings. modelType: Predictive / risk stratification adjunctive device output (Investigate Further vs Monitor) rather than direct diagnosis. ESS spectroscopy captures wavelength-dependent backscatter; preprocessing + proprietary neural network compares pattern against training data from histopathology-confirmed lesions; returns risk output to aid referral decisions.
